To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have undertaken a comprehensive microarray analysis of lung development and identified groups of genes that are coordinately expressed during this process.

the gene expression profiles of the entire process mouse lung development have been determined using microarrays and the expression patterns of extracellular matrix and other groups of genes have been analyzed.
the gene expression patterns of the extracellular genes in the lung are similar to the expression patterns in other developing tissues, but are also unique in the lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis, a devastating disease that results from the aberrant development of the lung.
the development of the lung and the molecular mechanisms that control this process.
understanding how the developing lung acquires its characteristic form and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data presented here is the first large-scale gene expression profiling of murine lung morphogenesis and provides a valuable resource for the pulmonary community.
the expression of the extracellular genes in the developing lung is highly regulated and coordinated.
this work provides an extensive resource for the pulmonary community and serves to identify novel genes that are expressed during lung development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a gene expression profile of the developing murine lung that will provide a foundation for future studies of lung development.
we have identified a large number of novel genes with pulmonary expression and have defined a large number of genes with extracellular matrix expression in the developing mouse lung.
we have identified a large number of genes expressed during lung development and have begun to define their expression pattern in the developing lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many more genes expressed in the developing lung than previously appreciated and the expression of these genes can be temporally and spatially defined.
the extracellular matrix (ECM) is not a passive scaffold but rather a dynamic, active participant in lung development.
we have developed a comprehensive gene expression profile of the entire process lung development.
